title: Unit 3 Stand-alone 5: COPD Nutrition Documentation and Negligence Review

question.stem: Which of the following entries in the client's medical record would help refute the charge of negligence?
question.preamble: The nurse that cared for a client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who lost more than 10% of ideal body weight has been named in a lawsuit charging negligence.

options.text: The client has been instructed to eat 3 large meals daily.
The client has been encouraged to maintain a high-calorie, high-protein diet.
The client has been encouraged to drink fluids with meals to promote digestion.
The client has been instructed to exercise 30 minutes before eating to improve appetite.

question.explanation: Encouraging a high-calorie, high-protein diet (Option 2) is the correct, evidence-based nutritional teaching for a client with COPD at risk for malnutrition, and documentation of this teaching would help refute a claim of negligent care. Instructing the client to eat 3 large meals daily (Option 1) is incorrect teaching, since large meals can cause abdominal distention that presses on the diaphragm and worsens dyspnea; smaller, more frequent meals are recommended instead. Encouraging fluids with meals (Option 3) is also incorrect, since fluids taken with meals can cause early satiety and reduce food intake; fluids should be taken between meals. Instructing the client to exercise immediately before eating (Option 4) is incorrect, since exertion before a meal increases fatigue and dyspnea and can further reduce appetite and intake; rest before meals is recommended instead. Documentation of these 3 incorrect teaching points would not help refute, and could support, a negligence claim.
